segments.t: The command palette finds and runs any command of the main window's menus when you type a few letters of its name, so you need neither the mouse nor the place of the command in the menus. It also runs the right-click commands of the terminal you are in, such as KTPH000Clear BufferKTPH001 or KTPH002ReconnectKTPH003, switches to any open tab, the ones you used last first, including the terminal tabs of your other korTTY windows, opens a tab for any saved or shared teamwork connection, and runs any snippet of the KTPH004Snippet ManagerKTPH005 in the terminal. It reaches every menu command while the menu bar is hidden and in terminal-only fullscreen.

Press KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 (KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on macOS), or choose KTPH018View → Command Palette…KTPH019. The same keys close it again.

The keys work in every tab of a main window, also while a terminal, a snippet editor or another tool tab has the keyboard focus, with the menu bar hidden and in terminal-only fullscreen. A tool that opens in a window of its own, instead of as a tab, has no palette.
Choose KTPH001View → Snippet Palette…KTPH002 to open it with KTPH000 already typed, listing only the snippets (see KTPH003Snippet paletteKTPH004).

On Windows and Linux korTTY keeps KTPH008KTPH000KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH001KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH002KTPH013 for itself, so it does not reach the program in the terminal, while plain KTPH014KTPH003KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH004KTPH017 (the previous command in bash) still reaches the shell. KTPH018KTPH005KTPH019 combinations, which arrive as KTPH020KTPH006KTPH021+KTPH022KTPH007KTPH023, are left alone too.

The palette opens at the top of the window with an empty search field. On macOS, when the menu bar of a window you closed is still shown, KTPH000View → Command Palette…KTPH001 opens the palette in the frontmost open window.
Type part of a command's name. The letters have to appear in that order but not next to each other, and case does not matter, so KTPH000 finds KTPH001New WindowKTPH002. Each row shows:
the command's name as its menu shows it, followed by its menu path in grey, for example KTPH000Dock LeftKTPH001 View › Live Journal;
a check mark when the command is a setting that is on, such as KTPH000Show DashboardKTPH001;
its keyboard shortcut, if it has one, also one you chose yourself in KTPH000Settings → KeyboardKTPH001.

The menu path is searched as well, which keeps the commands with the same name apart: KTPH000 finds KTPH002View › Live Journal › Dock LeftKTPH003, and KTPH001 finds KTPH004View › File Browser › Show on LeftKTPH005. A match in the name ranks above a match in the path, and among equally good matches the commands you chose recently come first.

With nothing typed, the palette lists the commands and connections you chose recently, up to eight and newest first, then the KTPH005open tabsKTPH006, and then every command, menu by menu. Other connections only appear once you type. KTPH007SnippetsKTPH008 never appear before you type, not even the ones you ran recently, because a snippet runs a command in the terminal. Next to the menu commands it offers KTPH009Next TabKTPH010 and KTPH011Previous TabKTPH012, which switch tabs like KTPH013KTPH000KTPH014+KTPH015KTPH001KTPH016 and KTPH017KTPH002KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH003KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH004KTPH022, and the KTPH023terminal and tab commandsKTPH024.

Typed first, a scope character limits the list to one kind of row: KTPH000 lists only commands, KTPH001 only tabs, KTPH002 only connections and KTPH003 only snippets, so KTPH004 finds the close commands but no tab whose name contains "close". The line below the list names these characters.
The list of recent choices lasts until korTTY quits; all windows share it and it is never saved. What you type into the palette is neither logged nor sent anywhere.

The palette also offers the commands of the terminal's and the tab's right-click menus that the menu bar does not have. They act on the terminal tab you are in, and the terminal commands on its focused pane, the one your typing goes to and that KTPH000Edit → Find…KTPH001 searches:

Clears the scrollback and the screen of the focused pane but keeps the prompt line, like KTPH004Clear BufferKTPH005 in the terminal's right-click menu. While a full-screen program such as KTPH000 or KTPH001 runs, it does nothing. On macOS the row shows the terminal's own key, KTPH006KTPH002KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH003KTPH009.
Opens a copy of the tab next to it and signs in like KTPH000DuplicateKTPH001 in the tab's right-click menu.
Connects the tab again, like KTPH000ReconnectKTPH001 in its right-click menu.

Watches the tab for new output after a quiet spell, or stops watching it, like the entry in its right-click menu; the row shows a check mark while the tab is watched. See KTPH000Watching a tab for activity or silenceKTPH001.
Watches the tab for output that stops, or stops watching it, like the entry in its right-click menu; the row shows a check mark while the tab is watched.

In any other kind of tab, such as a snippet editor, these rows are greyed out. KTPH001FindKTPH002 is not listed a second time: type KTPH000 for KTPH003Edit → Find…KTPH004, which opens the search of the focused pane.

The pane commands are not in this table because the menu bar has them: the commands of KTPH001View → PanesKTPH002 and KTPH003View → Multi-execKTPH004 are rows like every other menu command, with their menu path, shortcut and check mark. Type KTPH000 for KTPH005Split RightKTPH006 View › Panes, which splits the focused pane on its own server like KTPH007Split Right (same server)KTPH008 in the right-click menu, with the same progress dialog and the same KTPH009server policyKTPH010 check, and moves the keyboard into the new pane. KTPH011Split DownKTPH012, KTPH013Split PaneKTPH014, KTPH015Close PaneKTPH016, the focus commands, KTPH017Next PaneKTPH018, KTPH019Previous PaneKTPH020, KTPH021Zoom PaneKTPH022, KTPH023Broadcast to All Panes of This TabKTPH024 and the KTPH025Multi-execKTPH026 commands are found the same way and do exactly what their menu items do; a row is greyed out while its menu item is, so the commands that close, focus or zoom a pane need two or more panes. KTPH027Zoom PaneKTPH028, the broadcast command, KTPH029Include This PaneKTPH030 and KTPH031Include All Panes of This TabKTPH032 show a check mark while they are on, and KTPH033broadcast modeKTPH034 can always be switched off, also when only one pane is left.

Every tab of the window is a row with a KTPH001TabKTPH002 badge, named as the tab bar names it: the name you gave it with KTPH003Rename TabKTPH004, the title its shell set, or the name of its connection, without the group prefix and the connection status. The grey detail of a terminal tab names where it is connected, as KTPH000 taken from the saved connection (or the connection's name for a local shell), and its tab group, for example KTPH005root@db-01 · ProductionKTPH006. A program in the terminal can set the tab's title but not this detail, so a title that imitates another server does not hide where the tab really is; a long title is cut at half the row, so it cannot push the detail out of sight either.

The tabs are listed in the order you last used them, the most recent first, and when you type, equally good matches keep that order. The tab you are in comes last and is marked KTPH009Current tabKTPH010, so typing KTPH000 and pressing KTPH011KTPH001KTPH012 goes back to the tab you used before it. A tab counts as used when you select it, with the mouse, with keys such as KTPH013KTPH002KTPH014+KTPH015KTPH003KTPH016 or KTPH017KTPH004KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH005KTPH020, or from the palette. With KTPH021KTPH022KTPH006KTPH023+KTPH024KTPH007KTPH025 in this orderKTPH026 switched on, stepping through the tabs with KTPH027KTPH008KTPH028 held counts only the tab you stop at. Closing several tabs at once, regrouping them or dragging a tab to another place counts only the tab shown afterwards, not the tabs the selection passes over on the way. The order lasts as long as the window and is never saved.

The terminal tabs of your other korTTY windows follow, each window's tabs in the order they were used there, with the window's number in front of the detail, such as KTPH000Window 2 · admin@web-01KTPH001; a window's number is its place among the open windows, in the order they opened. Choosing such a tab brings its window to the front, restores it when it is minimized, and selects the tab there. Other kinds of tabs of the other windows, such as editors or AI results, are not listed.

Every connection saved in the KTPH002Connection ManagerKTPH003 is a row with a KTPH004ConnectionKTPH005 badge, named as the Connection Manager names it. The grey detail says where it connects, as KTPH000 (KTPH006Local ShellKTPH007 for a local shell), and its group, for example KTPH008postgres@db-01.example.org · ProductionKTPH009; a connection without a name of its own shows only its group there, because its name already is KTPH001. The detail never shows a password, a stored credential or an SSH key.

When your organization's policy allows KTPH001teamworkKTPH002, the connections shared with you follow, with KTPH003Shared (Teamwork)KTPH004 in front of the detail. Their names come from a file someone else writes, so their rows always name KTPH000 as well, even when the name looks like an address, and a long name is cut at half the row so that the detail stays in sight. Teamwork connections you deleted on this computer are not listed.

Saved connections are listed with the one you used last first, and the ones you never used by name; the teamwork connections follow by name. When you type, the connections you chose in the palette recently come first among equally good matches, and the others keep that order. Type KTPH000 to list only connections, the ones you chose in the palette recently first.

Choosing a connection opens a tab for it in this window and signs in exactly like KTPH000ConnectKTPH001 in the Connection Manager (see KTPH002Signing inKTPH003): korTTY checks the server policy first, then uses the saved password or key and asks only for what is missing. Cancelling a question opens no tab. Unlike the Connection Manager, a connection opened from the palette counts as used, so it moves up in the palette and among Quick Connect's frequently used connections.

A connection whose server or jump server your organization's KTPH000server access policyKTPH001 blocks is greyed out. Choosing it keeps the palette open, and the line below the list names the blocked server and says that your organization manages it.

Every snippet of the KTPH002Snippet ManagerKTPH003 is a row with a KTPH004SnippetKTPH005 badge, named as the library names it. Type part of its name, or of its folder, category or tags. Type KTPH000 first to list only snippets: the ones you ran from the palette recently come first, then the others, the most recently used first and the ones never used by name; among equally good matches the same order applies. The grey detail names the terminal the snippet runs in, for example KTPH006Run in root@db-01.example.org (prod-db)KTPH007: the KTPH001 of the pane's connection, then the tab's name. A program in the terminal can change the tab's title but not its connection, and the connection comes first, so a long title is what gets cut when the row is too narrow, never the server. Typing a tab's or a server's name does not list every snippet, because a snippet is not found by the terminal its row names.

Choosing a snippet runs it exactly like KTPH004Send to TerminalKTPH005 in the Snippet Manager: korTTY replaces its KTPH006placeholdersKTPH007, asks for a declared variable that has no stored value (cancelling sends nothing), sends it as a one-liner where the language allows, executes it with KTPH008KTPH003KTPH009, switches to the tab and shows KTPH010Sent to …KTPH011 in the status bar. It runs in the terminal tab you are in, or, when another kind of tab such as the Snippet Manager is selected, in the terminal tab you used last (or the only one that is open), and in that tab's focused pane: the pane you typed in last before you opened the palette, or the tab's first pane when that one has been closed. When the tab is split, the detail names the pane by its number, for example KTPH012Run in pane 2 of root@db-01.example.org (prod-db)KTPH013, and a pane that is a split to another server is named by its own KTPH000. Afterwards korTTY switches to the tab and gives that pane the focus. The snippet runs in exactly the pane its row named and is not mirrored to the other panes in KTPH014broadcast modeKTPH015 or a multi-exec group; if that tab or pane was closed in the meantime, korTTY says that no terminal is open instead of picking another one. While a full-screen program such as KTPH001 or KTPH002 runs in the pane, or a paste is still being sent to it, korTTY sends nothing and says that the pane is busy; it checks this before it asks for variables and again right before it sends.

Press KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 (KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013 on macOS) instead to open the snippet in the Snippet Manager without running it; the line below the list names this key while a snippet row is chosen. Without a terminal tab in the window the snippet rows are greyed out and say so, and KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 still opens them.
A snippet runs on the server at once

Choosing a snippet row executes the snippet in the named terminal straight away, with KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006, on whatever server that pane is connected to. Read the grey detail before you press KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008, and use KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH003KTPH012 to look at a snippet first. The palette never lists snippets before you type, so KTPH013KTPH004KTPH014 on an empty palette cannot run one.

KTPH004View → Snippet Palette…KTPH005 opens the command palette with KTPH000 already typed in the search field, so it lists every snippet and nothing else, the ones you ran from the palette recently first. Type to narrow the list; what you type is added after the KTPH001. Choosing a snippet runs it exactly as described in KTPH006Running snippetsKTPH007, in the focused pane of the terminal its row names, and KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 opens it in the Snippet Manager instead.

The Snippet Palette has no keyboard shortcut of its own by default, because KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 (KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on macOS) already opens the JobScheduler. Assign one in KTPH018Settings → KeyboardKTPH019; the page refuses a combination that another command or the terminal already uses. Like the palette's own shortcut, the one you choose then also works while a terminal has the focus, with the menu bar hidden and in terminal-only fullscreen, and pressing it while the palette is open closes it. On macOS, when the menu bar of a window you closed is still shown, KTPH020View → Snippet Palette…KTPH021 opens the palette in the frontmost open window.
Run the chosen row, or the first row when none is chosen
Open the chosen snippet in the Snippet Manager instead of running it; on any other row the same as KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002
Move between the search field and the list

The palette closes first and then runs the command exactly as its menu item does: a dialog opens, a setting such as KTPH000Show DashboardKTPH001 is switched, and KTPH002Edit → Find…KTPH003 opens the search of the active terminal. A tab row selects its tab, a connection row opens a tab for its connection, and a snippet row runs its snippet in the terminal it names. A click outside the palette closes it as well.

Commands that cannot run right now are greyed out, such as KTPH000Unlock Vault…KTPH001 while the vault is already open or KTPH002Rename Tab…KTPH003 outside a terminal tab.
